name: stata-research-guard
description: Author Stata workflows under general research-code rules, optionally reuse complete compatible templates, then lint and audit them.

interface.shortDescription: General-rule Stata authoring with optional complete templates.
interface.longDescription: Uses a curated and versioned Stata research-practice label corpus as optional evidence and preferred starting points, including AER and AEJ atoms for canonical summary datasets, descriptive Excel sheets, and grouped bar figures. General rules govern every substantive transition and every template selection, binding, adaptation, and verification. The selector compares the target with each template's six-field input profile, rejects known contradictions, chooses at most one alternative within a variant group, and composes distinct sequential transitions only when their state contracts connect. A template is selected only when permitted bindings leave the complete atomic transition intact. If its frame, algorithm, control flow, interface, or output contract must change, the result is no longer treated as a template: split at a natural state boundary when possible, otherwise use general_rule. When the user identifies an existing .do file as the canonical frame for a lightly adapted sibling, an estimator-agnostic clone template applies only declared literal edits and blocks every other difference. The search-ranked nearest inspected candidate may be retained only as a nonbinding hint for useful commands, ordering, state handling, or output idioms; rank never establishes compatibility. New reports record nearest_template_hint, template_status, and hint_used. Partial repair is the default, and only the final verified implementation matters. Harmless input loading, inspection, assertions, naming, logging, and setup are direct primitives. Missing template coverage is advisory unless strict reuse enforcement is explicitly requested. The plugin rejects loop depth three, unjustified or opaque depth-two loops, positional dispatch, unused options, one-use programs, dependency probes, manual event dummies, and coefficient reconstruction. Final Excel preserves the complete raw outreg2 table and adds only adjusted R-squared and the e(sample) dependent-variable mean. A workbook with one sheet uses direct outreg2 replace/append to an explicit .xls target; the canonical .xlsx formatter is reserved for two or more sheets in one workbook, including 2SLS first-stage groups. Event-study code uses explicit single-# factor-variable terms with the declared base omitted, exact raw e(b) tokens, bottom legends, raw outcome titles, and immediate PDF export. One outcome uses a no-loop automatic axis; multiple outcomes use one flat loop, with fixed or mixed axes only under the explicit compatible axis contract. Under report_policy=required the plugin records template and substantive general_rule spans in root report.md; optional permits omission, and disabled forbids creating or modifying it. Legacy report and manifest vocabulary is accepted only for read compatibility. Runtime success, static audit, and substantive validity remain separate. The plugin organizes and validates researcher code without deployment, dependency, or submission packaging.
defaultPrompt: Inspect this Stata target read-only and preserve compatible folders, files, entrypoints, call order, and estimate handoffs. Before writing or execution, list the exact folders and files to create or modify plus moves, renames, deletions, overwrites, entrypoint, and execution command, then wait for approval. For an overhaul, show one exact proposed tree and every new persistent variable with its reader-facing description, raw source unit plus exact formula or threshold, output unit and observation level, creation file, period/geography, coding/missing rule, use, and root README action; retain them there for researchers and label each persistent variable in its creation do-file. For a new applied-micro panel project or approved overhaul that needs preparation, summary, and estimation, use the unnumbered masters.do, build_analysis_panel.do, build_summary.do, and run_regressions.do spine; otherwise create only the requested stages and outputs. Do not add dependency, installer, deployment, or submission-package artifacts unless explicitly requested. Keep generated comments project-local and provenance in session or audit evidence. After approval, lint, audit, run the research workflow when requested, and verify the exact contracted outputs.

Audit this Stata project, including master files, data preparation, descriptive statistics, regressions, robustness, figures, and exports. Default to the active reachable entrypoint/call graph; use scope.mode all or project-relative scope.include_paths/scope.exclude_paths only when requested, prune excluded directories before discovery, and report unreachable files as inactive advisories. If multiple top-level masters remain plausible, return needs_review without arbitrarily selecting an active workflow. Block loop depth 3 or greater and any depth-2 loop that does not substantially reduce one repeated mechanical body over two plain axes; report structural depth 4 or greater as a review warning, separately from loop depth. Also block positional job-string dispatch. Prefer explicit sequential blocks or one readable flat loop, and use Excel, PDF, and .ster outputs without TeX.

Given only this natural-language research contract and declared inputs, build an independent Stata workflow. Do not use source code or prior outputs as an answer key. Make tables and figures consume the same named summary dataset, then run workflow_reproduction_check and keep runtime_success, static_audit, substantive_validity, numerical, valid-JSON, workbook-render, and PDF-render statuses separate. Multi-sheet and estimate multiplicity require project-level producer-consumer evidence isolated across disconnected workflow components; dynamic/runtime-only names are context_pending and nonblocking. Same-lineage derived/template evidence must be marked independent_support=false and excluded from independent external-evidence counts.

Decompose this Stata task only as far as the current input-to-output contract requires. Apply the general rules to every substantive transition and every template selection, binding, adaptation, and verification. Search the exact checkpoint for each reusable transition. Select one preferred_candidate or conditional_candidate only when permitted bindings leave the complete atomic transition intact. If frame, algorithm, control flow, interface, or output contract must change, stop calling the result a template; split at a natural state boundary when possible, otherwise use general_rule. If the user identifies an existing .do file as the canonical frame for a lightly adapted sibling, call plan_dictionary_repairs with source_reuse and planner include/exclude scope, clone first, apply only declared literal edits with exact occurrence counts, and require an exact candidate readback. Reject templates with known input-profile contradictions and do not splice alternatives within one variant_group. Retain the rank-relative nearest candidate solely as a nonbinding hint. Under report_policy=required, record nearest_template_hint, template_status, and hint_used in root report.md; optional permits omission and disabled forbids touching report.md. Harmless input loading, setup, inspection, assertions, naming, logging, and one-off inspection summaries may be written directly. When creating masters.do, list exact Project Inputs and Project Outputs at the top. Immediately above every individual direct `do`, `run`, or `include` call, add one contiguous comment block with exact Input, exact Output or Output: none, and a complete sentence explaining the called file's project-local role, then lint it with role master and authoring_state new. Keep each master stage call fail-fast: never use capture, nostop, or any literal or macro-expanded positional argument or option after the target; a shared directory-root macro may appear only as a complete directory component inside an explicit literal leaf path. Iteration is allowed and only the final frozen source is judged. Prefer one flat loop; permit depth two only when two plain axes repeat one mechanical body and substantially reduce duplication without hiding research or output choices. Never stack patches, wrappers, duplicate paths, depth-three loops, positional dispatch, registries, one-use programs, unused or future-facing options, unnecessary variables, manual event dummies, coefficient reconstruction, or project-specific frameworks. Before freezing, leave one implementation path per transition, verify every master call target and declared output, and require a template-reuse manifest only when the user explicitly requests that audit.

A direct master call may declare exact `Output: active dataset` only for a transient in-memory handoff to the next call; otherwise declare exact persistent output files or `Output: none`. Never list active dataset in the top-level persistent Project Inputs or Project Outputs inventory.
Never use `nostop` on any `do` or `run` call, including nested helper calls. A non-master helper may retain documented positional arguments, while the master remains an exact target-only shell.

Read and follow skills/stata-replication-workflow/references/general-rules.md before writing or adapting code. Select a writable template only when permitted bindings leave the complete atomic transition intact. If frame, algorithm, control flow, interface, or output contract must change, stop calling the result a template; split at a natural state boundary when possible, otherwise use general_rule. Retain the highest-ranked inspected candidate only as a nonbinding hint and state that nearest-by-ranking may still be absolutely distant or incompatible. Record nearest_template_hint=<label_id|none>, template_status=<no_suitable_template|wrong_selection|project_specific_contract>, and hint_used=<borrowed idea|none>. General rules may implement only an already-declared atomic input-to-output transition; they never supply an unresolved sample, estimand, merge key, treatment rule, model, event axis, sheet group, or output placement. Keep one readable final path and shallow indentation. Prefer one active loop; permit depth two only for substantial repetition of one mechanical body over two plain axes with visible research and output choices, and never use depth three. Do not add a registry, dispatcher, positional job string, one-use program, unused interface, dependency probe, manual event dummy, or coefficient reconstruction. In every newly created master do-file, write one language-appropriate complete role sentence immediately above each individual do call and lint with role master and authoring_state new; missing role prose is an error for a new master, a warning for a modified master, and not a retroactive block for an existing audited master. After final line numbers are stable, apply the selected report_policy. Under required, record and check caller-authored substantive authored_spans with confident one-based line bounds and record every selected template and substantive general_rule span; under optional, omission is allowed; under disabled, do not create or modify report.md. Harmless primitives are not rows. Legacy report vocabulary is read-only compatibility. Keep all provenance markers out of research .do code. Call audit_stata_project with the selected report_policy.

Use a typed named-sample-flow postfile only when the researcher supplies the checkpoint meanings and order; close it with postclose and never use it for coefficient reconstruction. Treat .ster replace seed, append, numbered load, readable store, and restore as separate estimate-lifecycle transitions.

Before selecting or writing regression Excel output, scan the complete data and estimate flow and record output_flow_profile: each outcome's meaning/label, unit and transform, sample and estimand, estimate handoff and specification order, evidence-backed reader-facing sheet_groups, and a substantive reason for every physical workbook/sheet placement. Define each semantic variable group once from labels, definitions, measurement relationships, and research purpose; names alone are not evidence. When each workbook has one sheet, keep direct outreg2 replace/append calls visible with an explicit .xls target and do not create a program, one-path global, unnecessary estimate store/restore cycle, scratch import/export, or Mata-only cosmetic block. Use the canonical outreg2_xlsx formatter with .xlsx only when one workbook requires two or more sheets, including separately grouped 2SLS first-stage results. Plan event-study axis_groups independently: automatic axes are the default, and only genuinely close, directly comparable outcomes under the same specification, sample, coefficient unit, and transform may share an evidenced fixed range.

Before retrieving code, decide whether this request needs code and classify its state-transition scale as no-write, atomic substep, checkpoint, multi-checkpoint, or explicit overhaul. Korean and English review-only/no-change intent (검사, 점검, 평가, 진단, 검토, 발전 가능성, 수정하지 않는다, review, audit, inspect, assess, diagnose, explain, do not modify) takes precedence over incidental add/improve/feature words and sets code_required=false and write_authorization.status=not_requested. Default to partial repair; accept overhaul only when the user's natural-language request is explicit or verified interface evidence makes it unavoidable. Convert only that footprint to dictionary headwords plus exact command, state, input-signature, and policy keywords, and load one compatible code block per selected headword.

Use a direct literal for a one-use binding and otherwise define or redefine a descriptive global in the consuming do-file. Keep only shared directory roots in masters.do; outcome-list globals belong in run_regressions.do. Use local only for lexical necessity inside a loop or program, temp objects, per-iteration scratch, or an immediately consumed r()/e() result. Never chain substantive aliases. In every regression command keep treatment or event window, controls, sample, fixed effects, weights, and VCE literal at zero substantive reference depth; one local outcome iterator in one flat loop is the normal exception. Format long enumerations as meaningfully grouped, whitespace-aligned multiline blocks. Use /// only when the next physical line continues the same command and omit it from the final line.

Preserve Stata's native coefficient names for factor-variable interactions and never generate aliases such as treat_y2015 or _y2015. In a conventional event-study RHS, omit the design reference and use compact selected levels such as i(2015/2018 2020/2024).year#1.treat2019 with one # only when the displayed minimum-to-maximum support has exactly one omitted interior reference. For an irregular window or a boundary reference, list every nonreference level as a flat native level-specific no-base term. Stata categorical factor levels must be nonnegative integers: recode signed relative time to a nonnegative factor index and restore negative relative-time text only in graph labels. Do not use invalid ibn(<numlist>) or ## there. A justified year##c.control heterogeneous slope inside absorb() remains separate. Verify every selected level against the exact raw e(b) token Stata returns; conceptual bn/b/o equivalence is not selector readiness. Keep observed raw names in outreg2 and event-study selectors, retain exactly one blank display-order slot for the omitted design reference, and derive x labels, zero reference position, and policy boundary from that slot. For exactly one outcome use a direct no-loop figure block; for two or more outcomes use one flat outcome loop. Place the comparison legend below the axis, put the raw outcome name alone at the top, and export each PDF immediately after its graph. Event-study graph text is English.

Keep every coefficient, standard-error, omitted/base, and note row emitted by outreg2 in native raw form. Do not filter, synthesize, rename, or reconstruct rows; only arrange order and sheet placement and add adjusted R-squared plus the estimation-sample dependent-variable mean. For one-sheet direct output, quietly summarize the dependent variable if e(sample), meanonly, bind r(mean) to a local, and use only adjr2 addstat(Dep. variable mean, that local). Apply the one-sheet direct versus multi-sheet formatter rule to 2SLS first-stage results without extra diagnostic rows. A declared baseline comparison covers every contracted outcome, sample, and specification.

Apply the report_policy contract consistently: code-writing plans and research_output_check default to required, standalone audit_stata_project defaults to optional, and disabled—including an explicit no-report request—must not create or modify report.md; require_report is only a compatibility alias for required when report_policy is absent. Master role findings use authoring_state (new error, modified warning, existing audit nonblocking). Native Stata python script <declared .py>, args(...) is explicit script integration, not a shell/winexec/bang/inline process escape or process_escape blocker, but its runtime success and outputs require separate validation.
